name: Dominica
summary: A green field with a cross of yellow, black and white stripes and a red disc in the centre showing a Sisserou parrot surrounded by ten green stars. It is one of only two national flags with purple, in the parrot's plumage.
origin: The playwright and artist Alwin Bully designed the flag for independence from Britain on 3 November 1978. Minor changes followed in 1981, 1988 and 1990, mostly to the order of the stripes and the colour of the stars.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun, the main agricultural products, and the Carib and Arawak peoples.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The fertile soil and the African heritage of the people.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The rivers and waterfalls, and the purity of aspirations.

symbols.name: Sisserou parrot
symbols.description: A purple and green Imperial Amazon parrot, endemic to Dominica.
symbols.meaning: The national bird; the flight toward greater heights.

symbols.name: Ten stars
symbols.description: Ten green five-pointed stars around the parrot.

symbols.name: Triple cross
symbols.description: A cross of yellow, black and white stripes.

facts: With Nicaragua's, it is one of only two national flags containing purple.
The Sisserou parrot is found only on Dominica and is endangered.
Dominica is often confused with the Dominican Republic.
clues: Green with a cross of yellow, black and white stripes and a parrot in a red disc.
One of only two national flags with purple.
Its ten stars stand for ten parishes.
